_readme: Every spoken line in Breath Coach, marked up for ElevenLabs. Line IDs match the recording script. Edit text here, re-run scripts/generate-voice.mjs, get new files with the same names. Never use more than two <break> tags in one line, and never end a line with one.

lines.text: Nothing to fix for the next four minutes. <break time="0.7s" /> We'll begin on your next breath.
Let the chair take your full weight.
You don't have to breathe well. <break time="0.6s" /> Just breathe along.
Make the exhale a slow pour, <break time="0.5s" /> not a push.
Somewhere on this breath out, let your jaw unclench.
Each exhale drops your shoulders a little further.
The day is over. <break time="0.7s" /> Tell your body — it's the last to hear.
Two more. <break time="0.6s" /> Make this one the softest yet.
Last one. <break time="0.6s" /> Empty all the way out.
Whatever's left of the day <break time="0.6s" /> it can wait until tomorrow.
Breathe in
Let it go
Before the phone, before the list. <break time="0.7s" /> We'll begin on your next breath.
Even in, even out. <break time="0.6s" /> Like drawing a slow circle.
No pushing. The rhythm does the work.
This pace is yours. <break time="0.6s" /> The day will try to change it.
Notice the turn at the top of the breath. <break time="0.6s" /> Smooth it.
Awake is not the same as wired. <break time="0.6s" /> This is awake.
One thing at a time today, <break time="0.5s" /> starting with this breath.
A few more. <break time="0.6s" /> Memorise this tempo.
Last one. <break time="0.6s" /> Carry it out the door with you.
The day gets to join your rhythm today — not the other way round.
Breathe in
Breathe out
Sit tall. Feet on the floor. <break time="0.7s" /> We'll begin on your next breath.
Four equal sides. <break time="0.6s" /> Nothing rushed, nothing dragged.
Feel your feet. <break time="0.6s" /> That's the ground you're standing on.
The holds are where the steadiness is built.
Same pace in, same pace out. <break time="0.6s" /> You set the tempo now.
Whatever's coming, <break time="0.6s" /> it gets this version of you.
Square by square, the noise loses interest.
Two more squares. <break time="0.6s" /> Keep them clean.
Last one. <break time="0.6s" /> Walk out of it steady.
The room hasn't changed. <break time="0.6s" /> You have.
Breathe in
Hold
Let it go
Stay empty
This takes ninety seconds. You have ninety seconds. <break time="0.6s" /> We'll begin on your next breath.
Two sips of air in, one long pour out.
That second sip pops your lungs open. <break time="0.5s" /> That's the trick.
The exhale is the valve. <break time="0.5s" /> Open it slowly.
You're not solving anything right now. Just releasing the grip.
Two more. <break time="0.5s" /> Longest exhales yet.
Last one. <break time="0.5s" /> Let everything leave with it.
Still a lot on your plate — but you're holding it with looser hands.
Breathe in
A little more
lines.note: Tightest timing in the product. If over budget, ship RV-CUE-SIP-ALT instead.

lines.text: More
Let it all go
Lie down. Let the bed do the holding. <break time="0.7s" /> We'll begin on your next breath.
Sink. <break time="0.8s" /> The bed can carry all of it.
Eyes closed, <break time="0.8s" /> if they want to close.
On the hold, do nothing. <break time="1.0s" /> Floating counts.
Let the exhale sound like a sigh. <break time="1.0s" /> No one's listening.
Each wave takes you a little further from shore.
You don't need to fall asleep. <break time="1.2s" /> Just stop holding yourself awake.
Nearly there. <break time="0.8s" /> Heavier now.
Last one. <break time="0.8s" /> Let it lower you all the way down.
If sleep comes, let it. <break time="0.8s" /> You're done here.
Breathe in
Rest here
Sigh it out
And now <break time="0.6s" /> let your breath come back to its own rhythm.
Take one normal breath. <break time="0.6s" /> Nothing guided. Just yours.

_notGenerated.breathSounds: Record for real — see §3.2 of the voice-and-sound-production-guide. TTS cannot hit exact durations and synthetic breathing is uncanny in a breathing app.
_notGenerated.cueTones: G4 392Hz / B4 494Hz / D5 587Hz from a sampled instrument or synth — see §3.3.
